units.function: Testing-policy note requiring a shared embedded-PostgreSQL helper so server tests use disposable storage and loopback ports instead of risking the live control-plane database.
units.dependencyDirection: Human test authors are directed from individual server tests to one shared database fixture helper; the helper, not this document, owns isolation behavior.
units.keyDataModels: No domain model; operational concepts are PostgreSQL process, throwaway data directory, reserved-safe loopback port and live control-plane database.
units.lifecycle: Before a database integration test, allocate isolated storage and port through the helper; run the test; clean up without connecting to the live service.
units.testAssessment: This is a ten-line policy document with incident provenance, not executable evidence. It identifies a high-value safety invariant but does not specify or verify refusal conditions, cleanup, parallelism, CI behavior or protection against externally supplied production connection strings.
units.designRationale: Centralize dangerous integration-test database setup after an incident so every suite benefits from the same production-data protection instead of constructing embedded PostgreSQL ad hoc.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed-cloud and self-hosted Company OS tests and migrations must never mutate customer or production databases, especially when FDE deployments expose varied local configuration and operators run validation in customer environments.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY until the helper implementation is audited. Adopt the invariant independently: integration tests may connect only to an explicitly test-marked local disposable database with unique data directory/schema, loopback-only endpoint and generated credentials; refuse known production/staging hosts and non-test database markers; make destructive fixture cleanup validate its exact target; test parallel workers, crashes and CI/container profiles.
units.responsibilityConflict: Accidental test writes to a live control plane can destroy responsibility evidence and customer data without any authorized human decision. The safety gate must fail closed and produce an attributable operator-facing diagnostic rather than rely on convention.
evidence: git history: 5a0c1979cf439d434c527de4935687a178be4b8e [codex] Add runtime lifecycle recovery and live issue visibility (#4419)
Documentation-only unit; no focused test exists and no implementation pass is claimed
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL risk identified: integration tests can otherwise reach the live control-plane PostgreSQL and mutate production state. HIGH evidence gap: the document does not prove the helper rejects production URLs/hosts, validates cleanup targets or isolates parallel workers. HIGH self-hosted/FDE risk: customer-local environments increase configuration ambiguity and demand explicit test-database markers. POSITIVE: the policy centralizes setup and records incident-driven rationale rather than leaving isolation to each test author.
